headline: La Mesa Dam Remains Above Overflow Level at 80.20 Meters
deck: PAGASA reported La Mesa Dam at 80.20 meters at 5 a.m. on August 11, five centimeters above its 80.15-meter overflow elevation.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: La Mesa Dam's water level stood at 80.20 meters at 5 a.m. on Tuesday, August 11, according to PAGASA figures reported by the Philippine Daily Inquirer. That was 0.05 meter, or five centimeters, above the reservoir's 80.15-meter overflow elevation.
Because La Mesa has an ungated spillway, excess water passes over the overflow level without a manual gate release and drains toward the Tullahan River system.

sections.heading: What communities should know
paragraphs: Low-lying communities downstream should continue following current PAGASA and local disaster-office advisories. Reservoir readings can change as rainfall and inflow change, so the 5 a.m. measurement is not a substitute for a live warning.
The Tullahan River passes through parts of northern Metro Manila before reaching Manila Bay, making downstream monitoring important while overflow continues.

sections.heading: Background
paragraphs: This article was first published on August 9 when La Mesa was above its critical level but still below overflow. It has been updated because the reservoir subsequently crossed the 80.15-meter overflow elevation.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: An overflowing ungated reservoir can add water to downstream channels during already wet conditions. Clear, current measurements help residents and local officials make timely preparedness decisions.

sections.heading: What happens next
paragraphs: PAGASA and local disaster offices will continue monitoring rainfall, the reservoir and downstream waterways. Residents in flood-prone areas should follow location-specific evacuation instructions if authorities issue them.
